newsitem.title: INDIA: India OVL ready to dilute stake in Vietnam field.
newsitem.headline: India OVL ready to dilute stake in Vietnam field.

text.p: India's ONGC Videsh Ltd (OVL) is ready to give up five percent of its share in a Vietnam gas project to Petrovietnam in return for a new production sharing contract, an OVL official said on Tuesday.
"OVL is willing to give five percent of its share to Petrovietnam to finalise the long-pending contract," the official, who requested anonymity, told Reuters.
Petrovietnam is seeking an additional 10 percent participation in the project prior to finalising the contract, Oil and Natural Gas Corp's (ONGC) chairman B.C. Bora told Reuters last week.
State-run Petrovietnam currently holds a five percent share in the project, Bora said.
OVL, a wholly-owned subsidiary of ONGC, has 55 percent equity and the remaining is held by British Petroleum Co Plc and Norway's Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil).
Bora told Reuters that OVL was willing to shed part of its share in favour of Petrovietnam for concluding the PSC. The BP-Statoil combine will also have to shed some of their shareholdings, he said.

Work on gas block 061, which is estimated to hold two trillion cubic feet (57 billion cubic metres) of natural gas, has been delayed due to protracted negotiations over the production sharing contract, Bora said.
He said another issue which remains unresolved is the landed price of the gas, which includes the price of natural gas and the cost of transporting it from the offshore block to the landfall point.
The ONGC chairman was optimistic of finalising the contract as well as price issue in the next two months.
"We are nearing an agreement and we hope to sign the contract in a couple of months. Immediately thereafter, the development plan will commence," he said.
The production sharing contract, which was signed in May 1988, was for crude oil and not for natural gas.
The contract needs to be renegotiated for natural gas since pricing, transportation and marketing of the two hydrocarbons is different, the OVL official said.
